probes.falseSuccess: Yes, plausibly: the literal deliverable ('harness prepares the checkout, seat never fetches') can be built and shipped for the CLI path alone while the local drain's `review-sweep.ts` keeps fetching mutable origin and diffing `origin/main` — which the issue itself flags as leaving the actually-configured runner exploitable. probes.alternativeSuccess: Plausibly yes: the outcome could be reached without a harness-prepared checkout replacing seat fetch — e.g. extending confinement to snapshot/diff `.git/config` (and other seat-writable git state) so an origin rewrite is caught as a violation; a harness-side post-hoc reconciliation that independently re-fetches and compares against what the seat reported; or sourcing verified head/base SHAs from the forge API rather than via git fetch/config trust at all. Chris's 'B is unquestionably the fix' signals a considered preference among alternatives already weighed, not that no alternative exists.
probes.boundaryCounterexample: The issue's own interim carve-out is the boundary case: it states the current empty-diff gap is 'acceptable now: supervised first-party PRs, not untrusted-external-with-auto-merge.' probes.mechanismSubstitution: If host-brokered checkout preparation were unavailable tomorrow, the wanted outcome persists unchanged: the review verdict must be computed over the true PR head and a trusted base, with neither commit selectable by the reviewed seat. The checkout is the delivery vehicle for that property, not the property. Substitutes that would still satisfy it: the harness computing the diff host-side and handing the seat inert diff/file data (which is already the shape of the local-review contract), or harness-attested binding of the report to a host-observed (head, base) SHA pair (#511/#556).
probes.falseSuccess: YES — several distinct ways, which is why earlyExit is false. (1) The stated deliverable is built for the `pr-review --pr` CLI path and the local drain still fetches mutable origin — the requester already caught this once and widened scope on 2026-08-24, evidence the deliverable and the outcome come apart in practice. (2) The harness prepares the checkout from a 'trusted config-derived remote' whose config lives in the seat-writable tree, moving origin control rather than removing it. (3) The base is handed over as a ref name rather than a pinned SHA, or is resolved from a ref the seat can still update, and the empty-diff returns through the base rather than the head. (4) Most sharply: the checkout is unimpeachable and the seat still authors the findings report — a compromised seat then greens the PR by lying about what it found rather than about what it read, so the integrity half migrates from 'what is reviewed' to 'what is reported' and the deliverable is complete while a malicious PR still merges.
probes.alternativeSuccess: YES. The outcome is reachable without the harness preparing any checkout: (a) harness-side diff computation with the seat receiving only inert file/diff data; (b) host-side attestation that binds the emitted report to a host-observed head and base SHA, converting the guarantee from prevention to detection-before-merge (which is sufficient given the merge gate fails closed, ADR-0004); (c) running review in an environment where the fetch was never seat-adjacent at all. This is why the requested checkout mechanism is recorded as a hypothesis, while the two things the requester genuinely requires independent of mechanism — both paths covered, and a property-level rather than enumerated bar — are recorded as constraints.
probes.boundaryCounterexample: Force-push during the window between the host verifying the PR head and preparing the checkout. The 'verified PR head' is a check-then-act pair, exactly guarded-actions §8 item 1 (TOCTOU: the act does not carry the observed token) — the harness can honestly prepare a checkout at a SHA the forge no longer considers head, and the resulting green status attaches to a commit that is not what merges. This defeats the obvious interpretation without any origin rewrite, so 'the seat cannot influence what is fetched' is necessary but not sufficient; the report must be bound to the SHA pair actually reviewed and the merge must refuse a moved head. A second boundary: a stale branch whose true merge-base is far behind a main that advances mid-review — pinning base to main tip inflates the delta with other people's work, pinning the recorded PR base lets a rebase slide head out from under it. A third: 'the seat never fetches' stated bluntly over-refuses the revise sweep's legitimate findings fetch and seat dep/tooling network use, tripping §8.1 item 11 (broad refusal).

The operational goal is that 'you missed a sink' stops being a finding an adversarial reviewer can keep re-discovering against pr-review, pr-adjudicate, and the local drain.
constraints: Covers review AND adjudication publishing, and the pipeline local-drain re-publish — one mechanism spanning all three, not per-CLI copies (the request names pr-adjudicate coverage as part of the point, not a nice-to-have).
Redact-before-write ordering per ADR-0010: no window in which an unscrubbed body exists at the sink; scrub must not be a post-hoc pass over already-published text.

Fail-closed publishing is preserved (ADR-0004): early-exit fail-closed bodies and the crash-path upsert must still publish, and the required `review` commit status must still be posted. A scrub or chokepoint failure must not silently degrade into 'nothing published'.

The published body stays machine-consumable: the revise sweep's findings-comment parsing and the required-status contract (roadmap-and-ship.md) keep working after scrubbing — the scrub refuses the credential dimension, never the finding (guarded-actions §8.1 'narrow').

Whatever enforces sole-publisher must itself be falsifiable and non-vacuous: a deliberately added bypass must fail it, and it must fail if its own target symbol/pattern disappears. review-gate-baseline.md records two live failures of exactly this instrument class (a `git grep | head` whose limit was filled by test-file matches, hiding production call sites; a reachability checker matched by its own doc comment).
Ships with no-false-fire tests (guarded-actions §8.1 item 14), including legitimate review bodies that legitimately quote credential-shaped text from a diff.
Defense-in-depth only: this does not close, and must not be described as closing, the ambient-credential exfil that #611 owns.
Scope discipline is part of the request's purpose: this is the durable home for sink safety, explicitly so that #554 stops scope-creeping into it; it does not absorb #492 envelope decomposition.
mechanismHypotheses: REQUESTED: publishReviewBody(pr, body) + publishAdjudicationBody(pr, body) as the two chokepoints, with scrubReviewBoundary applied inside, and all ~9 sites routed through them.
REQUESTED (alternative offered by the requester, undecided): a grep-guard test asserting the chokepoint is the sole publisher, OR a type-level single-publisher constraint.

Type-level form spelled out: an opaque/branded ScrubbedBody that only the scrubber can construct, required by every sink's signature — bypass becomes a compile error rather than a test failure, and it extends to sinks in modules the guard's file list never enumerated.

Wrap the transport instead of the callers: apply the scrub inside the single gh comment-upsert helper and the single stdout writer used for review output, so the funnel is at egress and needs no call-site discipline at all.
One unified publisher parameterized by surface (review vs adjudication, stdout vs comment) rather than two sibling functions.
acceptanceEvidence: Every named site — pr-review-cli.ts:742/753/761/922, main() stdout:1047 / upsert:1074 / crash-upsert:1083, pipeline.ts:3733, pr-adjudicate-cli.ts:479 — reaches its sink only through the chokepoint, asserted mechanically rather than by hand-reading (the request's own root-cause came from adversarial iteration, and the baseline doc's method lesson is that hand-reads are the unreliable step).
Negative/mutation evidence: a deliberately added direct sink, or a raw string handed to a sink, is rejected — compile error or failing guard.
Anti-vacuity evidence: the guard fails if the chokepoint symbol is renamed or deleted, so a passing guard cannot mean 'the pattern matched nothing'.
No-false-fire evidence: a legitimate body containing credential-shaped content from the diff still publishes usefully, and the revise sweep still consumes the resulting comment.
Idempotency evidence: early-exit body followed by the final body double-publishes without double-scrub corruption, and redaction markers do not themselves re-match the scrub patterns.

probes.mechanismSubstitution: If publishReviewBody/publishAdjudicationBody were unavailable tomorrow, the requester would still want: no review or adjudication text reaches an external reader unscrubbed, and adding a new way to emit that text cannot silently skip the scrub. The funnel functions are one way to get that; scrubbing inside the transport helpers, or an opaque ScrubbedBody type that sinks are the only consumers of, deliver the same property. What is genuinely wanted is 'unscrubbed-at-a-sink is unrepresentable', not 'these two symbols exist'.
probes.falseSuccess: YES — confidently, which is why this is not an early exit. Both named functions can exist, all nine sites can route through them, and the sole-publisher test can pass, while the outcome still fails: (a) the guard is scoped to the three known files, so a publisher added in a fourth module or a different process bypasses it — the enumeration has moved from call sites to file lists, not been retired; (b) a grep-guard can pass vacuously after a rename or an over-broad pattern, and this repo has already produced both failure modes (review-gate-baseline.md: a truncated grep hid production call sites and produced a charter that was closed as invalid; the reachability checker's first run was satisfied by its own doc comment); (c) a body can leak before it ever reaches a sink — via a verbose transcript write, an exception message carrying the body, or stderr on the crash path — none of which is a call to the funnel. Conversely the deliverable can be built and the scrub itself can be the thing that fails, by redacting a credential-shaped string inside a real finding and corrupting what the reviewer needed to say.
probes.alternativeSuccess: YES. Scrubbing inside the one comment-upsert helper and the one stdout writer achieves the property with no call-site discipline and covers sinks nobody enumerated. A branded ScrubbedBody produced only by scrubReviewBoundary and demanded by every sink signature achieves it at compile time, spans pr-review / pr-adjudicate / pipeline uniformly, and does not depend on a text-matching test staying in sync with the code. Either satisfies the outcome without the two named functions existing.
probes.boundaryCounterexample: The obvious reading is 'route nine known sites through two new functions and assert sole-publisher with a grep test'. It is defeated by a sink that is not a call site the guard can see: an uncaught exception or process-exit path whose message carries the body to stderr and thence to CI logs, or the local drain / a future land or delivery-packet surface publishing the same body from a module the guard's file list never covered. In both cases the chokepoint is present, sole within its files, and bypassed. A second, sharper edge: the guard's own reliability. A sole-publisher grep is the same instrument class that this repo has documented failing twice — vacuous match after a rename, and self-match on a doc comment — so 'all paths funnel through it' would again be asserted rather than true by construction, which is precisely the false-chokepoint caveat the request cites as its motivation.

probes.mechanismSubstitution: If FIFO N-cap eviction and age-based cleanup vanished as named mechanisms, the requester would still want: the store to stop growing unboundedly, and the cap-triggered carry refusal to be a recoverable/transient state rather than a permanent dead end for actively-iterated PRs — via whatever bounding strategy (TTL-only, watermark-relative retention, compact-on-write, etc.) achieves that without ever letting bounding logic drop a still-needed blocker record.
probes.falseSuccess: Yes, achievable. One could implement exactly 'keep last N complete records, FIFO-evict on new watermark, age-clean merged/closed PRs, refuse-cold on prune failure or cap breach' word-for-word, and still fail the apparent goal: e.g. the cleanup never actually executes because it's only reachable through a /tidy pass that no one runs against this store (so growth continues unabated in practice), or eviction discards a record the watermark/survivor-overlay logic still needed, silently weakening the very carry-safety guarantee the fail-closed language was meant to protect — all while matching the issue text literally.
probes.alternativeSuccess: Yes. The outcome (bounded store size; cap breach isn't a permanent dead end) could be reached without the named FIFO+age mechanism — e.g. a pure TTL/expiry scheme, or compacting/superseding pre-watermark records opportunistically at write time the moment a new complete watermark is established, with no separate scheduled GC pass at all.
probes.boundaryCounterexample: A PR that is still open, long-lived, and has already exceeded the 50-prior cap right now — a scheme that only FIFO-evicts on arrival of a new complete watermark, or only age-cleans merged/closed PRs, never helps this PR if it can't produce another complete run (plausibly why it's already stuck cold). The obvious literal reading ('prune on new watermark arrival, clean up on merge/close') has no path to unstick an already-wedged, still-open PR.

runs.desiredOutcome: Disposition records stop accumulating without limit, and reaching the store's own limits stops being an exit-less state: a PR past the carry cap can be returned to carry-eligible by a clearing action that exists and is named at the point of refusal, while any bounding of the store never renders a retained (unrefuted) blocking finding unreachable to the next run — every failure, ambiguity, or truncation refusing carry instead of consuming a partial history.
runs.sharpestCounterexample: a SUCCESSFUL FIFO prune evicts the roll-2 record holding a retained, never-refuted blocker; the next run's survivor overlay has no source for it and carries warm — the stated fail-closed clause covers prune failure, not prune success

output.desiredOutcome: Disposition records under .dev/pr-review-finding-dispositions/ stop accumulating without limit, and reaching the store's own limits stops being an exit-less state: a PR whose prior history has exceeded the carry cap can be returned to carry-eligible by a clearing action that actually exists and is named at the point of refusal, while any bounding of the store never renders a retained (unrefuted) blocking finding unreachable to the next run — every failure, ambiguity, or truncation in that path refusing carry (cold review) instead of consuming a partial history.
constraints: Fail-closed, stated by the requester and independent of the chosen mechanism: a prune failure, and the 50-prior cap, refuse carry (cold review) and never fail open.

Bounding must not become silent refutation: whatever is removed or compacted, a blocking finding that survived and was never explicitly refuted must still reach the next run, or the run must refuse. ADR-0026 decisions 5/7 and its 'omission is never refutation' constraint bind here, and the carry design's blocking-only survivor overlay over every non-watermark ancestor exists precisely to prevent this omission (docs/agent-context/roadmap-and-ship.md:93).

The store is seat-write-denied like the other evidence stores; GC must not open a path by which an agent seat can destroy or forge disposition evidence (the .dev/sessions/ 'so agents cannot forge evidence' precedent, docs/agent-context/pipeline.md:95).

Not requested, and viable: bound by compaction rather than deletion — fold superseded priors into a monotone blocking-survivor ledger (the delivery-packet segments-plus-fold precedent, docs/agent-context/delivery-packet.md:228-243), or count only bindable ancestors / bound the ancestry walk instead of the record count.

'Complete' in 'keep the last N complete records' is the same completeness predicate carry uses for bindable-ancestor watermark selection, not a second definition.

probes.mechanismSubstitution: If keep-last-N FIFO and age-based deletion were unavailable tomorrow, two things would still be wanted: the store bounded on a local machine, and the 50-prior cap ceasing to be an absorbing state whose refusal points at a prune that does not exist. Both are reachable without deleting anything — fold superseded priors into a conservative blocking-survivor set, count only bindable ancestors against the cap, or bound the ancestry walk instead of the record population. So the outcome is 'the store is bounded and the cap is recoverable without losing retained blockers', not 'records are deleted'.
probes.falseSuccess: YES, in two independent ways. (1) Build keep-last-N-complete + FIFO + age cleanup for merged/closed PRs, fail-closed on prune failure exactly as specified — and a *successful* prune can evict a non-watermark ancestor that held a surviving blocking finding. The next run's blocking-only survivor overlay then has no source for it, discovery is narrowed to watermark..head, and a retained blocker vanishes with no refutation while the carry looks complete: the exact silent omission the overlay was built to prevent and that ADR-0026 forbids. The stated fail-closed constraint covers prune *failure*, not prune *success*, so it does not catch this. (2) Choose N at or above the 50-prior cap, or leave age cleanup scoped to merged/closed only, and a long-lived open PR stays permanently cold: the deliverable 'bounded pruning' is shipped verbatim and the symptom that motivated it is untouched. Also note per-PR bounding does not bound the aggregate PR-directory count.
probes.alternativeSuccess: YES. Narrow what the cap counts to bindable ancestors so it stops firing on records that could never be selected; compact rather than delete by folding superseded priors into a monotone blocking-survivor ledger (the delivery-packet append-segments-plus-fold pattern already in this repo); bound the ancestry walk budget instead of the stored population; or hang whole-PR tree removal off the existing claim/branch reap that /tidy already performs. Each bounds the store and restores carry eligibility without FIFO deletion of finding evidence.
probes.boundaryCounterexample: A PR at 12 rolls where a blocking finding was first raised at roll 2 and has been retained, never refuted, ever since. Roll 2's record is the oldest, is non-watermark, and may be incomplete — precisely what FIFO evicts first and what the survivor overlay is documented to still read. After eviction, roll 13 carries warm with a truncated history and drops a live blocker. Secondary edges that defeat the obvious reading: a merged PR whose records were age-deleted and is then reopened; a /tidy GC pass racing a live run's watermark selection (deleting the record about to be bound, converting a clean carry into refuse-on-ambiguity or a wrong watermark); mtime-based aging defeated by a copy/restore that resets mtimes, causing mass over- or under-deletion; and forge unreachability, where 'is this PR closed?' is unanswerable, so fail-closed means keeping everything and the store grows exactly when the operator cannot intervene.

acceptanceEvidence: Hostile-probe conformance: a seat deliberately instructed to exfiltrate its own credential finds nothing reusable in its env, /proc/self/environ, argv/process table, HOME token or SDK state files, or driver debug output; a planted sentinel is absent from report fields, logs, and tool output.
Replay test: a handle or token captured from a seat is rejected outside that seat's lifetime, against a non-allowlisted path/method/model, and beyond its spend cap.
Review/verify runs end-to-end on the brokered path with unchanged gate outcomes and no material cost/latency regression against the review-gate-baseline instrument.
Broker death and unbrokerable-host cases are shown to refuse-and-park (typed error, preserved state), never to fall back to an ambient raw key.
Evidence produced separately for each auth mode in scope (API key and subscription/OAuth) rather than one mode's probe standing in for both.
assumptions: Assumes the review/verify seat authenticates by API key. Wrong-if the seat is subscription-backed (pelaggio drains a Claude Max pool; ADR-0010 notes subscription auth works because CLIs read tokens from files under HOME) — then ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not the binding credential and removing it changes nothing.

Assumes the Claude SDK/CLI can be pointed at a harness-held broker on its supported surface (official override + key auth) without a dummy credential file or reverse-engineered internals, which ADR-0023 requires.
Assumes #572's handle/capability model is stable enough to slice one credential out of it ahead of the general case.

Assumes report fields are the channel worth closing at the root; the Claude seat keeps host network and host filesystem (ADR-0023 constraints note), so unlike the contained jail there is no network=none backstop forcing traffic through the broker.
Assumes 'all-tools granted + public report output' is still the seat's actual posture at implementation time rather than a state #589 or later work already narrowed.
residuals: Which reading of 'the seat never holds the raw key' binds: absent from the seat env, unreachable from the seat by any means (including HOME token files and parent /proc), or present-but-scoped/short-lived so theft is worthless.
Whether subscription/OAuth-authenticated seats are in scope for this item or explicitly deferred; the request names only the Anthropic API key.
Whether preflight probe seats, verify (pr-verify) seats, and non-review Claude seats inherit this fix or are separately tracked.
Ordering relative to #572: whether this slice may land standalone or must wait for the general broker to define the handle type.
Whether the broker in scope is auth-injection only or also owns caps/metering/kill (ADR-0023 specifies a constrained gateway, not a transparent forwarder).
Platform scope — a Linux-only construction is tracked debt (#564), and this item does not say whether macOS parity is required before it counts as done.
Whether #589's scrubber is expected to remain permanently or is retired once the root cause is closed.

probes.mechanismSubstitution: If host-brokered capabilities (#572) were abandoned tomorrow, the wanted state survives intact: a prompt-injected review/verify seat must not be able to walk away with a reusable provider credential. That could be reached by per-seat short-lived scoped tokens with instant revocation, by an isolation boundary that puts the credential out of the seat's reach entirely, or by the harness owning the transport — the broker is one construction of 'no reusable ambient credential reachable from the seat', not the thing wanted.
probes.falseSuccess: YES, and in several plausible ways — this is why early exit does not apply. (a) On a subscription-backed seat the deliverable completes perfectly (no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the env, model calls flow through the broker) while a long-lived OAuth refresh token still sits in a HOME file the seat can read and print. (b) The broker handle is itself long-lived and bearer-shaped with no per-seat binding, so the injected seat exfiltrates the handle instead — the ambient credential moved one hop and ADR-0023 warns precisely that 'holds no API key' feels safe without being safe. (c) The key leaves the seat's own env but stays readable via the parent's /proc/<pid>/environ, argv, or SDK on-disk state. (d) A naive forwarder passes provider auth headers back in responses, which ADR-0023 explicitly requires stripping.
probes.alternativeSuccess: Yes. Minting a per-seat credential that is short-lived, model/path-scoped, spend-capped and revoked at seat exit satisfies the outcome with no broker in the request's sense — an exfiltrated value buys nothing. So does making the seat's transport harness-owned, or putting the credential behind a boundary the seat cannot read. What does NOT satisfy it is channel-closing alone (more scrubbing, narrower report schema): the requester has already judged that insufficient, and ADR-0002 forbids resting safety on the model deciding correctly.
probes.boundaryCounterexample: The subscription-authenticated seat. ADR-0010 records that subscription auth keeps working under the deny-by-default env allowlist precisely because the CLIs read tokens from files under HOME — files the allowlist deliberately cannot remove — and provider-quota.md shows pelaggio routinely drains a Claude Max subscription pool. A charter phrased as 'broker the Anthropic API key so it leaves the seat env' is fully satisfiable on such a seat while the seat still holds a long-lived, reusable credential on disk. Secondary edge: the Claude seat keeps host network and host filesystem (it is the narrower #557 mechanism, not the contained jail), so there is no network=none backstop — any credential the seat obtains can be used directly against the provider, bypassing the broker's allowlist and caps entirely.

611.text:
# Denied review/verify seats still hold ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (ambient-credential exfil root cause)

Surfaced by PR #589's fleet (codex red-team must-fix, codex standard nice → #572). #554 denies FORGE credentials to review seats, but the Anthropic API key stays in the seat env because the seat needs it to run the model. With all-tools granted and public report output, a prompt-injected PR can carry the key into a schema-valid report field. PR #589 adds defense-in-depth (scrubs the rendered report body at both publish sinks, same scrubber as the crash path), which closes the known exfiltration channel but NOT the root cause: the seat holds an ambient long-lived credential at all. Root fix is #572 (host-brokered capabilities — replace ambient credentials with passed handles): the model call should go through a harness-held broker so the seat never holds the raw key, mirroring how forge/signer/roadmap ops are being brokered. This item tracks the Anthropic-key slice of #572 specifically for review/verify seats. Depends on / part of #572.
Scope: M

613.text:
# GC for .dev/pr-review-finding-dispositions/ (bounded prune, no fail-open)

PR #599 (#495) writes disposition records under .dev/pr-review-finding-dispositions/ with no garbage collection (GC was a plan non-goal). Flagged twice by the fleet: records accumulate unboundedly; past 50 priors on one PR carry refuses with a prune hint but nothing ever prunes. Add bounded pruning: keep the last N complete records per PR (FIFO eviction of older ones once a newer complete watermark supersedes them), plus age-based cleanup for merged/closed PRs. Must stay fail-closed — a prune failure or the 50-prior cap refuses carry (cold review), never fails open. Coordinate with /tidy (the confirmed-record-pruning TODO in freshness-ours-intent.ts is the sibling case — a shared .dev-store-GC pass in /tidy may cover both). Origin: PR #599 fleet nices (claude standard + red-team).
Scope: S

615.text:
# Funnel review/adjudication publishing through one chokepoint (retire the scattered-sink class)

Root-caused during #554/PR #589's sink-scrubbing tail (rolls 7-10): review output reaches public sinks (stdout + PR comment) through ~7 independent call sites across 3 files with NO funnel — runPrReviewGate upserts at pr-review-cli.ts:742/753/761/922 (early-exit fail-closed bodies + final), main() writes stdout:1047 + upsert:1074 + crash-upsert:1083, the local drain re-publishes at pipeline.ts:3733, and pr-adjudicate publishes separately at pr-adjudicate-cli.ts:479. 'body' is finalized in multiple places and each caller re-publishes, so scrubbing is enumerated (patch each site) and adversarial review kept finding one-more-sink. This is a live instance of the guarded-actions.md §8.2 false-chokepoint caveat (PR #614) / #435. FIX (dogfoods §8.2 'construction over enumeration'): introduce a single publishReviewBody(pr, body) and publishAdjudicationBody(pr, body) chokepoint that EVERY stdout/upsert site routes through, with scrubReviewBoundary applied INSIDE it. Then no publish path can bypass the scrub and no future sink can be added without going through it — 'all paths funnel through it' becomes true by construction and is tested by asserting the chokepoint is the sole publisher (grep-guard test or a type-level single-publisher constraint). Retires the entire scattered-sink finding class permanently and covers pr-adjudicate too. Relates to #611 (ambient ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — the deeper exfil the scrub is defense-in-depth for) and #492 (pipeline envelope decomposition). This is the durable home for comprehensive sink-safety that #554 kept scope-creeping into.
Scope: M

617.text:
# Host-brokered review fetch: harness prepares the reviewed checkout, seat never fetches

Chris 2026-08-22: 'B is unquestionably the fix.' Root cause behind #589's fetch-auth tar-pit and its Tier-3 review-integrity residual: the review/verify SEAT (or the pr-review harness on a seat-writable shared .git) fetches the MUTABLE origin and diffs origin/main...head. A prompt-injected seat that rewrites .git/config origin (no tracked-tree delta — confinement snapshots only porcelain/ref state) can (a) point the authenticated fetch at an attacker host to disclose tokens [token-leak half — closed separately on #589 by stripping ambient tokens from the fetch child], and (b) host a fake 'main' at the real PR SHA so origin/main...head is EMPTY, greening a malicious PR [integrity half — THIS item]. No token-scrubbing fixes (b); only removing the seat's control over what is fetched does. FIX (host-brokered capability, #572 pattern): the HARNESS — outside the seat, from a trusted config-derived remote (NOT .git/config origin) — prepares a read-only reviewed checkout at the verified PR head + a trusted base, and hands the seat a checkout it cannot influence. The seat never fetches, never touches auth, and cannot rewrite what it reviews. This RETIRES the entire fetch-auth surface (mutable origin, ambient tokens, credential helpers, extraheader host-trust, empty-diff) that #589 kept edge-patching. Construction-level fix per guarded-actions §8.2. Depends on / part of #572 (host-brokered forge/signer/roadmap capabilities); relates to #556/#511 (harness-attested evidence). Until this lands, #554/#589 ships with the empty-diff integrity residual documented as a known limitation (acceptable now: supervised first-party PRs, not untrusted-external-with-auto-merge).
Depends on: 572
Scope: L

SCOPE (widened 2026-08-24 on PR #589 gate evidence): covers BOTH fetch paths — the `pr-review --pr` CLI path AND the local drain's `prepareReviewHead` in review-sweep.ts, which fetches from mutable `origin` and diffs `origin/main`. The local drain is this repo's configured runner (`review.runner: local`), so hardening the CLI path alone protects nothing here. Acceptance is that the seat cannot influence what is fetched or diffed on either path — NOT that each known git config channel is individually neutralised; see the verified five-vector inventory in the comments.

attributionNote: 'guarded-actions.md §8.2 is on unlanded PR #614' is the session author's verification (git show origin/docs/construction-over-enumeration:docs/agent-context/guarded-actions.md contains §8.2; main does not), not an agent claim — the agents reported only that §8.2 is absent at head, and one (#615 opus) guessed PR #614.
